epigraph: Stone waits for the hand that names it.
vignette: The ground here is hard. It does not yield to roots. It rejects the glass trees of the Verdant. A player drives a fist of black stone into the dirt. The rock rises. It is heavy. It is cold. It stays. The Verdant tries to grow over it. The roots hit the obsidian and stop. The truth of the stone is simple. It is hard. It does not move. The Umbral players push more stone. The stack grows. The Verdant writes grass. The grass breaks on the rock. The rock remains. The ground believes in the weight. The Aspect of Outcrop is pure conviction. It holds the line. It does not kill. It simply refuses to be anything else. The Verdant must write something softer or leave. The stone is stubborn. It leans toward the ember cities. It likes the heat. It likes the weight of the spire. It is a block. It is a wall. It is the foundation of the stack. The Rift breathes near. The stone does not fear the leak. It is solid. It is here.
codex_note: The Outcrop serves as an immutable anchor in contested zones, resisting overwriting through sheer structural permanence rather than active hostility.
